newsitem.title: USA: Olympic Steel to build $22 mln Iowa plant.
newsitem.headline: Olympic Steel to build $22 mln Iowa plant.

text.p: Olympic Steel Inc said Wednesday it plans to build a $22-million temper mill, sheet processing and plate burning facility in Bettendorf, Iowa.
Ground-breaking is expected place in August, it said. The plant will serve the Iowa, Missouri, Nebraska, Kansas and Southern Illinois markets, it said.

The facility will include an area measuring 170,000 square feet that will house a Herr-Voss cut-to-length line, a four-high temper mill supplied by Intergrated Industrial Systems, and multiple pieces of plate burning equipment, the company said.
Michael Siegal, chairman and chief executive officer, said the facility continues the company's efforts to diversify geographically.
"Demand for the tempered steel product is increasing and this new facility will answer customers' demands for higher tolerances and flatness requirements," he said.

The company said it expects the plate processing equipment to be operational in the first half of 1998 and the temper mill and cut-to-length line by the second half of 1998. The plant will initially employ about 50 people.

"Our initial temper mill in Cleveland is currently running at full capacity and generating high gross margins. Based on our experience, this second temper mill should see even stronger results," Siegal added.
Timothy Morrison, a former hot and cold rolled marketing manager for Bethlehem Steel, has been appointed manager of the new plant, he said.
